types.title: Builder types
types.subtitle: Explore the 16 ways people work with coding agents.
types.howBody: Four observed preferences combine into a builder type. The letters describe a working pattern, not a fixed identity — each can shift as your habits and tools change.
types.galleryHint: Choose a portrait to see how its four preferences shape the way it builds.

M.name: Map
M.description: Frames the target, constraints, and route before moving
M.agentTip: Give the agent a written brief and explicit acceptance criteria

E.name: Explore
E.description: Reduces ambiguity by making progress and learning from what moves
E.agentTip: Start with a useful probe, then tighten the brief from what you learn

D.name: Direct
D.description: Stays close to the process and shapes the path step by step
D.agentTip: Ask for visible checkpoints and intervene when the path drifts

A.name: Delegate
A.description: Defines the boundary, then lets the agent choose the path
A.agentTip: State outcomes and constraints clearly, then leave room for autonomy

F.name: Focused
F.description: Gives one active agent or thread full attention
F.agentTip: Keep one goal in flight and make the next handoff unambiguous

W.name: Swarm
W.description: Keeps several agents or threads moving in parallel
W.agentTip: Split work by clear ownership and create deliberate convergence points

S.name: Systemize
S.description: Invests in tools, rules, and infrastructure that improve future work
S.agentTip: Let the agent capture reusable automation and durable operating knowledge

H.name: Ship
H.description: Optimizes for completing and delivering the product in front of you
H.agentTip: Keep the finish line visible and require a concrete delivered outcome
